name: Upstream indices update
query: Update the repository's indices for all ten Core AI upstreams without risking a partial refresh.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Run update script: node shared/scripts/update-upstream-indices.mjs
Step 2: Read source metadata from CORE_AI_UPSTREAMS rather than maintaining another hard-coded source list
Step 3: Fetch all ten Core AI upstreams: Core, Gutenberg, WordPress/ai, MCP Adapter, PHP AI Client, WP AI Client, Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and the WP↔Gutenberg map
Step 4: Fetch and normalize every response before writing any index; one failed source must leave every committed index untouched
Step 5: Confirm the existing Core, Gutenberg, AI plugin, MCP Adapter, PHP AI Client, and version-map indices are updated
Step 6: Confirm output written to shared/references/wp-ai-client-releases.json
Step 7: Confirm output written to shared/references/ai-provider-anthropic-releases.json
Step 8: Confirm output written to shared/references/ai-provider-google-releases.json
Step 9: Confirm output written to shared/references/ai-provider-openai-releases.json
Step 10: Verify deterministic formatting, numeric version sorting, stable-only GitHub releases, and bounded recent lists
Step 11: Parse the mapping by the WordPress Version and Gutenberg Version header labels even when Gutenberg is the first column
Step 12: Before opening a refresh PR, run node eval/harness/run.mjs --skip-upstream-drift so expected marker drift is the only skipped gate
Step 13: Generate upstream-drift.md with --format markdown --allow-drift and generate the source inventory from CORE_AI_UPSTREAMS
Step 14: Include and upload both reports, and use UPSTREAM_SYNC_TOKEN when configured so normal pull_request checks can run; disclose the GITHUB_TOKEN fallback

Step 15: Keep exactly one scheduled upstream-maintenance workflow: upstream-sync.yml owns the weekly cron and ai-skill-maintenance.yml runs only on workflow_dispatch or the upstream-release repository_dispatch
Step 16: Keep the two refresh branches distinct: upstream-sync.yml uses chore/core-ai-upstream-indices and ai-skill-maintenance.yml uses chore/ai-maintenance-upstream-indices

Step 17: Transfer no workspace or index artifact between jobs; publish only the canonical state hash built from complete per-source index fingerprints by node shared/scripts/ai-generate-updates.mjs --print-state-hash
Step 18: In every consuming job, rerun the deterministic updater and fail closed when the recomputed state hash differs from the refresh job's
Step 19: Treat missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_MODEL as a redacted advisory skip that still opens the deterministic index pull request
Step 20: Open no AI-authored skill pull request while detected changes carry taggedFiles: []
success_criteria: All ten registry-owned JSON files are updated in shared/references/
List sizes are limited for performance
Mapping output contains at least one row and includes WordPress 7.0.X mapped to Gutenberg 22.6
Drafts, prereleases, GitHub error objects, empty stable arrays, and missing Packagist packages cannot replace good indices
Any fetch or normalization failure happens before the first index write
A changed-index PR is self-validating and names every independently stale skill without claiming alignment
A no-change manual rerun creates no pull request
Exactly one upstream-maintenance workflow declares a schedule
The deterministic and advisory paths use two distinct refresh branches: chore/core-ai-upstream-indices and chore/ai-maintenance-upstream-indices
No job uploads or downloads an index or workspace artifact; jobs converge by recomputing the canonical SHA-256 state hash over complete normalized content for every source
A state-hash mismatch between the refresh job and a consuming job fails the run instead of publishing a mixed snapshot
A repository without AI credentials still refreshes indices and reports a redacted skip category
No workflow job can open an AI-authored skill pull request
